USE CASE
scientific-educational

ASSET
Complete publication-grade scientific figure rendered end to end, including every label and all typography.

PURPOSE
Show the exact reported effects of the leading colic interventions on daily crying and fussing time versus placebo, including the contradictory results for Lactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938.

CAPTION CONTEXT — DO NOT RENDER INSIDE THE ARTWORK
Title: What moves the needle on colic crying

STYLE PROFILE
Nature-inspired quantitative figure
A figure-native quantitative composition whose exact geometry, scales, uncertainty, and denominators are the visual focus.

FRAMING
Context: article
Do not render the title or subtitle inside the artwork; the surrounding article caption supplies them.

TYPOGRAPHY — HARD REQUIREMENT
- Render every character in Arial throughout; Helvetica is the only acceptable visual fallback.
- Text colour: #1A1A1A. Minimum readable text at 1,536 px width: 18 px; body 20 px; local headings 24 px; compact standalone title 31 px; panel letters 27 px.
- Use Arial throughout; Helvetica is the only acceptable visual fallback.
- Use sentence case and black or near-black labels.
- Use bold only for panel letters and short panel headings.
- Never use serif, condensed, outlined, beveled, or shadowed type.

CANVAS
- Background: #FFFFFF
- Aspect: 3:2 landscape unless the data require another ratio
- Margin: 7% clear outer margin
- Density: Compact, aligned panels with enough room for axes and uncertainty

PALETTE
black #1A1A1A, grey #767676, light grey #D9D9D9, blue #497FA6, pale blue #AFCFE0, muted green #669E83, pale green #BDD8C8, muted orange #C88F43, salmon #CA756B, lavender #A79AC4

VISUAL LANGUAGE
- Use black axes and tick marks, explicit units, exact uncertainty marks, and direct labels where space permits.
- Use colour-blind-safe solid colours only to distinguish datasets.
- Use no background gridlines; if a reference line is scientifically necessary, keep it thin and light grey.
- Use simple panel boundaries only when they clarify different denominators or scales.
- Keep all non-data illustration subordinate to the plotted evidence.

ARCHETYPE
quantitative — Show verified numerical estimates, uncertainty, scales, and denominators with geometry that is mathematically faithful.

COMPOSITION
- Use a standard plot form appropriate to the values: dot-and-whisker, line, bar, or scatter.
- Label axes and units and include tick marks; do not use background gridlines.
- Use direct labels or a compact key with black text and coloured swatches.
- Keep incompatible scales or denominators in clearly separated panels.

EVIDENCE-BACKED STORY
- The individual-participant meta-analysis of four double-blind trials reported 25.4 minutes per day less crying and fussing with L. reuteri DSM 17938, driven by breastfed infants.
- The largest single trial, which uniquely included formula-fed infants, reported 49 minutes per day more crying and fussing in the probiotic group.
- Pooled lactase-drop trials reported no significant effect.
- All three estimates carry wide 95% confidence intervals; populations and feeding modes differ, so the rows must be read as separate experiments, not one pooled effect.

DIRECTLY OBSERVED
- All plotted values are the reported adjusted mean differences and 95% confidence intervals from the cited publications.
- The Sung 2014 estimate is the trial's reported 49 minutes per day more crying or fussing in the probiotic group at one month.

INFERRED, MODEL-SUPPORTED, MIXED, OR UNCERTAIN
- The contrast between the pooled estimate and the largest trial reflects the breastfed versus formula-fed difference reported in the individual-participant meta-analysis.

TOPIC-SPECIFIC LAYOUT
- Single open panel on a white landscape canvas: three horizontal dot-and-whisker rows over one shared linear minutes-per-day axis.
- A dashed vertical reference line at zero labelled '0 = no difference'; directional cues 'less crying' left and 'more crying' right under the axis.
- Row labels and study details in black Arial at the left; each exact estimate printed beside its dot.
- Compact key at the bottom expanding the dot, whisker, and CI encodings.

SCIENTIFIC CONSTRAINTS
- Arial throughout; smallest text at least 26 px at a 1536 px canvas width.
- Dot positions and whisker endpoints must be proportional to the supplied axis.
- Do not pool the rows visually or imply one combined effect.
- Keep the title outside the artwork because this is an article figure.
